title: Take out the catch-all
starter:
type suit = Hearts | Diamonds | Clubs | Spades
type card =
  | Number of int * suit
  | Jack of suit | Queen of suit | King of suit
  | Ace of suit
  | Joker

let points (c : card) : int =
  match c with
  | Number (n, _) -> n
  | _ -> 10
hints: The `_` case answers 10 for every card that is not a `Number`. Which cards should not get 10?
Replace `| _ -> 10` with cases that name constructors. Several can share one line: `| Jack _ | Queen _ | King _ -> 10`.
After the faces, add `| Ace _ -> 11` and `| Joker -> 0`. With no `_` left, the compiler will tell you about the next card someone adds.

answer.code:
type suit = Hearts | Diamonds | Clubs | Spades
type card =
  | Number of int * suit
  | Jack of suit | Queen of suit | King of suit
  | Ace of suit
  | Joker

let points (c : card) : int =
  match c with
  | Number (n, _) -> n
  | Jack _ | Queen _ | King _ -> 10
  | Ace _ -> 11
  | Joker -> 0
answer.explain: The reference names every constructor: `Number (n, _) -> n`, `Jack _ | Queen _ | King _ -> 10`, `Ace _ -> 11` and `Joker -> 0`. With no catch-all, adding a constructor later makes the compiler warn at this match.
